ety.text: Late 19th century, originally dialectal northern English, from a euphemistic alteration of hell.

ex: Heck, what did I expect? It's too muddy out to go biking today.
You can go to heck as far as I'm concerned.
"And the railway industry needs a heck of a lot of people to be up-skilled," notes Darroch.

senses.d: The bolt or latch of a door.
A rack for cattle to feed at.
A door, especially one partly of latticework.
A latticework contrivance for catching fish.
An apparatus for separating the threads of warps into sets, as they are wound upon the reel from the bobbins, in a warping machine.
A bend or winding of a stream.

it:diamine.gl: an expression of wonder, impatience or irritation

es:caray.gl: crikey, wow, good heavens, golly, gosh, whoa, man, boy, blimey (expresses surprise, asto…

ety.text: Borrowed from Catalan carall. Doublet of carajo. Cognate with Portuguese carai.
From Ecclesiastical Latin, Late Latin diabolus (possibly semi-learned), itself from Ancient Greek διάβολος (diábolos).

chain.g: warrior with the qualities of Hector

ety.text: From Hector (“in Greek and Roman mythology, a character in Homer’s Iliad who is the greatest warrior of Troy”), from Late Middle English Hector (“warrior with the qualities of Hector”), from Latin Hectōr or Ancient Greek Ἕκτωρ (Héktōr), from ἕκτωρ (héktōr, “holding fast”), from ἔχειν (ékhein), present active infinitive of ἔχω (ékhō, “to have, own, possess; to hold”), from Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold; to overpower”). The verb is derived from the noun.

senses.d: Sometimes in the form Hector: a blustering, noisy, turbulent fellow; a braggart, bully.
To dominate or intimidate in a blustering way; to bully, to domineer.
To behave like a hector or bully; to bluster, to swagger; to bully.

grp.label: to behave like a hector or bully

ety.text: Borrowed from Medieval Latin intimidāre (“to make afraid”), from Latin in (“in”) + timidus (“afraid, timid”).
Borrowed from Late Latin tyrannizāre, borrowed from Ancient Greek τυραννίζω (turannízō). By surface analysis, tirano + -izar.
